units.name: Atlas

tier.basis: The registry gives this game no tech tiers: its eras are periods of history, not gates that unlock units.

cost_band.basis: Units are not bought during play in this game's registry entry; forces are balanced by weight class and points values. The design has a C-bill price, but no band uses it.

mobility.notes: Top speed of the tabletop AS7-D from the BattleTechWiki, divided by the Centurion CN9-A reference's top speed: a little over four-fifths of the reference, so slow. The game has no standard tank to compare with; among 'Mechs it is one of the slowest standard designs, and most enemy 'Mechs can outrun it. MechWarrior Online's stock AS7-D, with its standard engine, is slightly slower again and uses the game's heaviest movement profile. Handling keeps the two-legs default (pivot): the legs turn the body while the torso twists on top, and no source shows it sliding sideways. No jump jets.

body.notes: An assault 'Mech at the very top of the standard weight range, with arms, working hands and the famous skull-shaped 'Death's Head' cockpit. The size list puts medium to assault mechs in large; huge is kept for giants two tanks in size and superheavies. Its hands and weight make it a strong brawler in the game-wide physical attacks, and its Battlefists quirk (optional tabletop rules) adds a to-hit bonus to punches, a numbers-only effect. Its Distracting quirk makes nearby enemies' morale checks harder under the optional morale rules, also numbers only, so it is not recorded as an ability.

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class order decided: the registry's armour map gives heavy for the Assault 'Mech weight class that the BattleTechWiki infobox lists. It carries nearly as much armour as some light 'Mechs weigh, among the most of any 'Mech. Zonal is game-wide (locations and critical hits, registry note); in MechWarrior Online foes aim at its right torso, because losing it also loses the arm hanging from it and both their weapons. Directional: the BattleTechWiki says the plating is especially thick on the front of the chest and on the legs, and the rear torso armour is thinner than the front (see uncertain). It has no ammunition protection (CASE); the AS7-K variant adds it.

sensors.notes: The registry gives no sight figures for this game, so the band is the medium proposal. Standard 'Mech sensors give no trait. Its Improved Communications quirk (optional tabletop rules) lets it ignore the weakest level of enemy ECM sensor ghosts, a numbers-only effect. The head has room for a small folding satellite dish for long-range communication.

armament.name: Autocannon/20 (Defiance 'Mech Hunter)
armament.summary: The huge right-torso autocannon. In MechWarrior Online one shot can cripple a lighter 'Mech, and each shot is followed by a pause to reload. On the tabletop it reaches only about three-fifths as far as the reference autocannon. It feeds from a small ammunition bay (the fiction speaks of a ten-round magazine) and, without a cooling jacket, it runs hot. In the tabletop fiction weapons of this class fire single shells or bursts depending on the maker; the piloted version, which the series rule picks, fires one shell at a time.

armament.name: LRM 20 (FarFire Maxi-Rack)
armament.summary: The left-torso long-range missile rack. In MechWarrior Online it fires homing missiles after a target lock; enemy ECM blocks the lock unless the Atlas closes in, a teammate holds TAG on the target, or a teammate's PPC hit shuts the ECM down for a moment. It can also fire indirectly at targets that spotters hold, so it hits enemies it cannot see itself. Inside its minimum range it does almost no damage. Its tabletop reach is a little under one and a half times the reference autocannon's. Its big salvos use up ammunition fast, and firing it alongside other large launchers adds MechWarrior Online's extra heat. In the tabletop fiction the rack ripple-fires its missiles in waves.

armament.name: SRM 6 (TharHes Maxi)
armament.summary: A six-tube short-range missile launcher in the left torso, beside the LRM rack, with a limited stock of reloads. No cited page says its missiles steer, so it is coded as unguided rockets. Its tabletop reach matches the autocannon's.

armament.name: Medium lasers (Defiance B3M, four)
armament.summary: Four medium lasers on one entry: the two arms carry a laser apiece, and a centre-torso pair points backwards to discourage flankers. They need no ammunition but add heat. Their tabletop reach matches the autocannon's. MechWarrior Online's stock AS7-D lists the two centre-torso lasers without marking them as rear-facing.

crew.notes: One MechWarrior pilots it. In the fiction it served as a command 'Mech, and its Command 'Mech quirk (optional tabletop rules) gives its side a small initiative bonus, a numbers-only effect. Dual-cockpit refits, which add a second seat, are not the stock design. It is not an OmniMech, so friendly battle armour could ride it only with magnetic clamps; riding is left off (game-wide).

on_death.notes: A 'Mech that players pilot in MechWarrior Online: when it is destroyed, the player goes back to pick a 'Mech for the next drop. No cited page describes an ejection, a death explosion or a wreck to recover for this design.

strengths.why: Carries nearly the most armour of any 'Mech, so it soaks enormous punishment and keeps shooting back.
The heavy autocannon can cripple a lighter 'Mech with a single good hit.
Two rear-facing lasers punish flankers who get behind it, and the lasers need no ammunition.
The LRM rack lets it hit at long range and fire indirectly in support of teammates.
Working hands and sheer weight make it better than most 'Mechs in the game-wide physical attacks.

weaknesses.why: Ponderously slow: most enemy 'Mechs can outrun it, and running away is their best chance against it.
Losing the right torso also loses the right arm and the guns in both, so enemies focus fire there.
Apart from the LRM rack, every weapon reaches only a short way, so it must close in to use most of its firepower.
Its LRMs do almost nothing to an enemy that gets close.
The autocannon and both launchers feed from small ammunition stocks, and the big LRM salvos run dry quickly.

countered_by.why: Faster 'Mechs choose when to fight and escape before its short-reach guns can bear.
An ECM-equipped foe keeps its LRMs from locking on unless a teammate tags the target or the Atlas closes in.

counters.why: Light and medium 'Mechs, which the game rates as medium armour, can be crippled by one autocannon hit; the fiction has a lone Atlas able to destroy a whole battalion of light Stingers.

combos.why: A teammate holding TAG on a target keeps its LRMs locked, even through enemy ECM.
A teammate's PPC hit switches off enemy ECM for a moment, opening the target to its LRMs.
Spotters that find and hold targets let it fire its LRMs indirectly from behind cover.

units.memorable: BattleTech's skull-faced giant: the heaviest standard 'Mech, armoured like a fortress and built to frighten, with an autocannon that cripples lighter 'Mechs in one hit.
units.as_player: A slow, towering brawler. Left mouse fires the heavy autocannon, right mouse the lasers (two guard your back) and a third button the short-range missiles; hold a lock on a target, or on one a teammate spots, to send the LRM rack over cover. Twist the torso to aim, watch heat and ammo, and stay near allies: fast enemies will dance around you, and losing a side torso takes its arm with it.

sources.note: The wiki retells the Technical Readouts in its own words with page references, so it is not official text. Gives the weight class, top speed, weapons and their placement, ammunition, rear-facing lasers, armour distribution in words, hand actuators and the design quirks.

uncertain.note: The Master Unit List, where the registry says the official unit role lives, refused every request (HTTP 403 behind a browser check), so roles step 1 found no official line and steps 2 to 5 decided.

No cited page says which weapon group the pilot has selected at spawn. The autocannon is primary as the weapon the BattleTechWiki lists first; the MechWarrior Online page lists an arm laser first in its stock loadout.

Cannon rests on MechWarrior Online firing one heavy slug per shot (the cited page's one-shot wording, and the wiki's Weapons page, read but not cited, which says Inner Sphere autocannons fire a single shell). The BattleTechWiki's Autocannon/20 page, read but not cited, says weapons of this class fire singly or in bursts in the fiction; read that way it would be an autocannon, with no atypical break.
The reach comes from the BattleTechWiki's Autocannon/20 page (read, not cited for lack of room): its long range is about three-fifths of the reference autocannon's, so short.

By its tabletop reach (BattleTechWiki LRM 20 page, read, not cited) it is medium, a little under one and a half times the reference. It is coded off-screen because the cited pages say it can fire indirectly, at targets spotters hold, which the off-screen rule names as a reason on its own.

Lock-on weapons list only what they lock onto. The cited pages name only enemy 'Mechs as lock targets, so only ground vehicles are listed; on the tabletop, which has no lock step, the launcher can fire at any ground target.
The reach comes from the BattleTechWiki's SRM 6 page (read, not cited): the same tabletop long range as the autocannon, so short. That page also says SRMs lack sophisticated guidance.
The reach comes from the BattleTechWiki's Medium laser page (read, not cited): the same tabletop long range as the autocannon, so short.
The tabletop design points two centre-torso lasers backwards; the MechWarrior Online page lists two centre-torso lasers without saying which way they face. The entry follows the design.

Low air and naval rest on the series having VTOLs and naval vehicles on the tabletop, not on the cited pages; infantry rests on the tabletop and on MechWarrior 5: Clans' Elementals. The same holds for the SRM and laser entries.

No cited page gives per-location armour values. Directional rests on the BattleTechWiki's remark that the front of the chest is especially thick and on the game's separate front and rear torso armour.
No cited page describes this 'Mech's destruction; respawn follows the rule for a unit players pilot in a game where they return after dying.

Read but not cited for lack of room: the BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans page (the Atlas is not among its playable 'Mechs, so that title fills no field here), its Long-Range Missile page (calls LRMs self-guided and able to fire indirectly), its List of Design Quirks (the effects of the four quirks), and the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Weapons and Autocannon 20 pages.

fit_notes.note: The sources stress the LRM rack's indirect fire support, but the siege coding rule says a long-range missile alone is not siege, and its lock-on delivery is not lobbed. Anti-armour comes only from the lock-on rule leaving the LRM able to hit nothing but 'Mechs.
A missile rack that is medium by reach but fires indirectly over cover at spotted targets: the off-screen and lobbed terms each cover half of this.
The damage map turns Ballistic into kinetic, while the fiction describes armour-piercing high-explosive rounds; the cannon family allows only armour-piercing or explosive.
One laser entry holds two forward lasers in the arms and two that only cover the rear; the mount list has no way to say which arc a weapon covers.

atypical.note: The registry's damage map turns the autocannon's Ballistic hardpoint type into kinetic (damage step 4, and the registry note names autocannons as kinetic), while the piloted version fires one heavy shell at a time, which makes it a cannon; our cannon family allows only armour-piercing or explosive damage.
